description: We are a team of curious minds and aspiring explorers fascinated by the mysteries of our universe, the origins of Earth, and the science behind the world around us. We believe that every great discovery starts with curiosity, creativity, and the courage to ask questions. We are looking for enthusiastic, open-minded, and friendly people who enjoy exploring new ideas, solving problems, and working together. Skills in programming, data analysis, scientific research, graphic design are welcome!
summary:
FIRE IN FREEFALL is an interactive educational program designed to raise awareness about fire safety in space and the unique behavior of flames in microgravity.

Fire behaves differently in space than it does on Earth. A fire abroad a spacecraft can become a serious threat to astronauts, especially in an enclosed environment. Since unexpected situations can occur during any space mission, astronauts need access to reliable information and safety guidance.

Our project combines scientific information, artificial intelligence and interactive features. It includes an educational section explaining how fire behaves in microgravity, the potential dangers of spacecraft fires, and the importance of fire prevention. One of its main features is an AI assistant that allows users to ask questions and receive clear, accessible answers about fire in space and established safety procedures.

We have also developed themed fire characters and interactive elements to make learning more engaging and memorable. 

Our goal is to make complex scientific information accessible, improve awareness of potential space hazards, and demonstrate how AI can support astronaut training and education. 

We believe FIRE IN FREEFALL can become a valuable additional educational tool for astronauts, researchers and anyone interested in space exploration. Because safety in space begins with knowledge and preparation.
details:
FIRE IN FREEFALL is a web platform that explores how fire behaves in space. It uses NASA research and scientific data to explain how flames change in microgravity, how fire spreads, and how it can be extinguished.

Our platform includes a NASA Research Explorer, an interactive 3D Fire Lab, data analysis tools, a fire risk analyzer, a scenario simulator, and an AI assistant that helps users explore scientific information.

The main advantage of our project is that it brings scientific research and interactive visualization together in one place. We want to make complex space research easier to understand and help people explore fire safety challenges for future missions to the Moon and Mars.

We used Python, FastAPI, JavaScript, WebGL, and AI development tools such as Claude and OpenCode. Our team focused on scientific accuracy, usability, data reliability, and making the experience engaging.

What makes our project creative is the combination of NASA research, interactive fire visualization, and data analytics. Instead of only presenting scientific information, we let users explore and better understand how fire behaves beyond Earth.
dataRefs: Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data
